meaning: Lamna, Greek lámna, a voracious fish or shark; ditropis, from Greek dýo “two” and trópis “keel”, i.e. double-keeled, referring to the rudder-like projections on either side of the tail
description: A stocky North Pacific cousin of the porbeagle and great white, dark grey above and white below, with a short cone-shaped snout, a large first dorsal fin and a double-keeled tail stalk. Adults usually carry dark blotches on the belly, and the diet is mostly salmon, squid and other fish.
depth: Surface to about 650 m, usually less than 150 m
